name: Photonic Pressure Cannon PPC-2 'Sunburn'
description:
The Photonic Pressure Cannon generates an intensely focused beam of coherent light in the near-ultraviolet spectrum, but its primary mechanism of harm is not thermal — it is mechanical. By rapidly pulsing the beam at frequencies between 800 and 1200 pulses per second, the PPC-2 creates a phenomenon called laser-induced plasma pressure: each pulse ionizes a thin layer of surface material, and the explosive expansion of that plasma generates a localized pressure wave equivalent to a repeated physical impact. Against unarmored targets, this produces deep subcutaneous bruising, ruptured capillaries, and in sustained exposure, structural damage to underlying bone. Against light armor, it can cause spallation of inner surfaces.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS developed the PPC-2 as a crowd-control alternative to kinetic impact rounds, marketing it to municipal contracts across the GLMZ administrative zones. The pitch was that it left no ballistic evidence and produced 'compliance injuries' rather than lethality. Field deployment rapidly disproved the lethality claim — sustained bursts to the torso have proven fatal in multiple documented incidents, and the weapon's reputation for 'clean' crowd suppression collapsed within two seasons of its municipal rollout.

The weapon is recognizable by the distinctive purple-white glow of its emitter array and the sharp cracking sound each pulse makes — not unlike rapid applause at close range. Targets who have survived describe the sensation as being hit repeatedly by an invisible fist that somehow leaves no visible entry point. Forensic physicians in the free clinics have taken to calling the characteristic injury pattern 'Arcturus bruising.'
specifications:
effective range: 40m (pressure effect), 80m (thermal/flash effect only)
pulse rate: 800–1200 Hz (adjustable)
power source: ARCTURUS Photon Pack AP-3 (20-second continuous burst capacity)
weight: 4.7 kg
length: 72 cm
emitter array: 7-element near-UV coherent array
cooling system: Passive radiative fins with thermal cutoff at 340°C
burst modes: Single pulse, Sustained beam, Area scatter (experimental)
tactical_use: Municipal units use the PPC-2 for dispersal operations, typically sweeping the beam across crowds in short bursts to drive movement without (officially) causing lethal injury. Military and black-market operators have discovered that sustained torso exposure at high pulse rates is reliably fatal within 8–12 seconds, making it effective for executions that resist standard forensic classification. The weapon's lack of projectile evidence and unusual injury pattern make it attractive to operators who need kills that don't look like kills.
cultural_context: The PPC-2 is deeply associated with municipal overreach in the political consciousness of GLMZ's lower districts. Protest movements have adopted stylized imagery of the weapon's purple glow as a symbol of institutional violence. Several prominent activists bear 'Arcturus bruising' scars they display publicly. Conversely, in upper-tier corporate enclaves, the weapon is seen as a responsible alternative to lethal force — a perception that ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS continues to aggressively cultivate despite the mounting injury record.
story_hooks: A municipal officer's PPC-2 was used in a fatal crowd suppression event. The weapon's serial number traces back to a unit that was officially decommissioned two years ago. Someone is running a ghost inventory.

A forensic physician at a free clinic has quietly documented 34 deaths with Arcturus bruising patterns over 18 months. She's been offered significant money to lose her records. She hasn't decided yet.

ARCTURUS is lobbying to have the PPC-2's injury classification changed from 'potentially lethal' to 'compliance instrument.' They've already secured three council votes. Two more and the municipal contracts expand city-wide.
A resistance cell has acquired a crate of PPC-2 units and is debating whether to use them, destroy them, or make their existence public. They've asked a fixer to broker the decision.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular rifle-form factor with a distinctly asymmetrical profile. The barrel assembly dominates the forward section, housing the visible emitter array behind a translucent UV-resistant shroud. The stock is compact and utilitarian, designed for one-handed sweep operations. Overall impression: surgical precision mixed with crowd-control brutality.
physical_description.dimensions: 72 cm length overall, 8 cm width at emitter housing, 6 cm height at stock. Emitter array occupies forward 18 cm of barrel section.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced—4.7 kg distributed across the frame creates a forward-heavy feel that demands both hands for sustained aim, though brief bursts can be managed single-handed by trained operators.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with brushed aluminum alloy barrel shroud and internal emitter housing. Thermal management fins are anodized steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray on the polymer body with dull brushed aluminum on the emitter shroud. Passive radiative fins show a slightly aged anodized patina. No gloss—built for function, not appearance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with silver-gray aluminum accents. The only bright element is the internal purple-white glow visible through the emitter window during charging.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized tactical polymer with fine horizontal texturing for all-weather grip. The fore-grip is wrapped in thin black synthetic cordage for precision control during sweep operations.
distinctive_features: Seven-element emitter array visible through a beveled, UV-resistant transparent shroud—the core of the weapon's lethality
Passive radiative cooling fins running the length of the barrel shroud, angled for maximum heat dissipation
Thermal cutoff indicator: a thin red-line thermometer strip along the left side of the barrel that darkens at 340°C operational limit
Charging port and ARCTURUS Photon Pack AP-3 coupling on the underside of the stock, recessed and armor-protected
Safety selector lever integrated into the trigger guard with three positions: Safe, Single Pulse, Sustained (with an unmarked fourth detent for Area Scatter mode)
Faint ionization residue—a faint ozone smell and occasional bluish crystalline buildup—visible around the emitter shroud on heavily-used units
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo stamped in small serif lettering on the left side of the stock. Serial number and municipal contract ID engraved on the underside of the barrel shroud in tiny numerals. The name 'SUNBURN' is stenciled in faded orange lettering below the charging port—street nomenclature that has stuck, not official branding.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained units show minimal wear; the emitter shroud remains clear and the fins unobstructed. Heavy-use municipal and black-market examples display light discoloration around the emitter window from sustained ionization, wear patterns on the grip from repeated handling, and the thermal indicator strip often darkened halfway up from chronic overheating. Field-damaged units may have cracks in the shroud or scorch marks from emergency thermal cutoffs.
